p: The TRIP Resurgence project aims to rescue an old forgotten IETF protocol called TRIP (Telephone Routing over IP) that was imagined by the designers of SIP, the VoIP protocol.
The project came around as a member of UwUtel shared this protocol on the community, and other members that liked the idea of using TRIP for telephone routing in UwUtel, including the admin.

Unfortunately this protocol never caught on in the world of Telcos, and there is only one publicly available archived implementation of it (others were known but are lost to time now). So we have to implement a TRIP Routing Daemon (or Location Server in TRIP terms) ourselves. This is the main project.
ARFNET Internet Services ARFNET Internet Services
tripd is the TRIP Resurgence Location Server implementation, a telephone routing daemon.
As far as we know, it is the only modern maintained implementation in existence, as we aim to implement all of the protocol by 2027 hopefully.
tripd is being written in C11 and built with CMake, with as little dependencies as possible, currently zero.
Development is happening in the tripd Github organization repository
An example configuration is provided in the repo root as tripd.conf
Currently only development builds are supported
When tripd is production ready we will make tarball releases and packages for Debian at least.
The Telephony Routing over IP protocol, RFC 3219, is an application layer policy-based dynamic routing protocol for telephone prefixes very similar to how BGP is for network prefixes.
TRIP has similar sessions, messages, attributes and route selection algorithm to BGP.
It first appeared in the IETF in 2001, as a real alternative for routing in telephone networks.
